articles.title: Trump’s Iran Strategy Reaches a Critical Crossroads After Midterm Defeat
articles.description: President Donald Trump spent the final weeks of the US midterm campaign predicting that the war with Iran would end "right after the election." With the votes now in, his Republican Party is reeling from losing both chambers of Congress in a rout that his own vice president blamed squarely on the conflict. "The reason we lost is the war," Vice President JD Vance wrote on X on November 4. Trump called the assessment "largely true" but said he would make the same decision again because “you can’t let Iran have a nuclear weapon.”…

articles.title: Europe's Grid Spending Is Up 155% Since 2019
articles.description: Most European countries expect higher investments in their grid infrastructure through 2030 after more than doubling annual investments since 2019, the European Union Agency for the Cooperation of Energy Regulators (ACER) said in a report on Friday. A total of 22 out of 24 countries reviewed in the report raised annual investments in grids last year compared to 2019, with a 155% increase on average, ACER said in its Monitoring Report, Energy infrastructure development in Europe 2026. articles.title: Oil Prices Plunge as U.S. Elections Shake Up the Iran War
articles.description: December WTI crude oil is headed for one of its roughest weekly losses in months after the market shed $11.37, or 11.10%, from its opening price of $102.39. Prices posted a weekly high at $102.75 before breaking sharply to $86.65. Early Friday, the contract was trading near $91.58, still down heavily for the week. The decline was not driven by a sudden collapse in demand or a surprise rise in inventories. articles.description: Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL), a major Indian state-owned refiner, is struggling to hire tankers to transit the Strait of Hormuz and pick up cargoes in the Gulf, chairman Vikas Kaushal has told Bloomberg. articles.title: ADNOC Expands LNG Empire With Major New India Supply Deal

articles.title: China’s Carbon Emissions Plunge 3.1% as Oil Demand Slumps
articles.description: A decline in fuel use in China’s industrial sector has led to a 3.1% decline in carbon dioxide emissions in the third quarter of the year, the Finnish climate outlet Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air has reported, as cited by Reuters. The lower emissions from the world’s largest generator of CO2 resulted from a 4% drop in crude oil consumption, CREA said, adding that fuel use in transport dropped even more markedly, by 9% in the three-month period. articles.description: The global crude oil market is moving back towards oversupply, according to analysts from Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan, with demand destruction from high prices causing fears of a deficit to fade and concerns of a glut to rise. “We estimate the global oil market returned to a surplus of 1.1 million barrels per day ‌in September, widening to 1.4 million bpd in October, nearly matching last year's average of 1.3 million bpd,” JP Morgan said in a report this week.
